### 1 Sensors for human interaction

#### 1.1 FB Light Switching Sensor Basic (Object Type 421)

##### 1.1.1 Aims and objectives
###### The FB Light Switching Sensor Basic is used in the Application Domain Lighting for providing input data to switching actuators. It specifies the functionality, for example contained in a switch or a push button, to switch the switching actuator on or off.

 Display elements (with own FBs) can be integrated to show the status of the switching actuator.

 The inputs and outputs of the Functional Block are described but not the Human Machine Interface (HMI). Consequently, the manufacturers of the button or switch have the possibility to implement their design and their operation methods.

##### 1.1.2 Functional specification

###### 1.1.2.1 Overview The FB Light Switching Sensor Basic provides hardwired inputs for triggering transmission of values of output Datapoints.

FB Light Switching Sensor Basic FB Switching Actuator Basic

IOO SOO SOO IOO

###### Figure 1 – Basic communication model (example)

 1.1.2.2 Parameter On Off Action The parameter On Off Action shall limit the values transmitted by the output SOO to either only 0 (“Off”) or 1 (“On”).

 This mainly makes sense if an appliance is realised as a combination of two FBs LSSB each with one interaction point. This realisation however is only meaningful if the parameter ETM is not implemented or has the value “Disable”.

###### The dashed outlined areas realise the same functionality. The DP SOO in the left solution sends both On and Off. The DPs SOO in the right solution only send either On (e.g. upper FB) or Off (e.g. lower FB).

 1.1.2.3 Toggle Mode Toggle Mode denotes the behaviour where the value of the outputs SOO inverts on each transmission. The value of SOO can be calculated by the device internally or by interpreting the received value of the input InfoOnOff (IOO).

 The concept of toggle mode is only meaningful in the realisation as given in Figure 3. In case the parameter Enable Toggle Mode (ETM) has the value Enable, the parameter On Off Action (OOA) becomes meaningless.

###### Figure 4 – Toggle Mode without IOO Figure 5 – Toggle Mode with IOO


###### Rule 1

 Each subsequent transmission on the DP SOO will have an inverted value compared to the previous transmission.

 SOOn+1 = NOT(SOOn)


###### Rule 2

 Rule 1 is in this case extended with the following: on each reception of IOO, SOO becomes the value of IOO. 

 SOO = IOO


-----

###### The relation between IOO and Toggle Mode (Figure 5) can be summarized in the following pseudo code.

if(Update(DP_IOO)) {// This is rule 2.
DP_SOO = GetValue(DP_IOO);
}
if (UserInteraction) { // This is rule 1.
DP_SOO = InvertValue(DP_SOO);
SendValue(DP_SOO);
}

###### 1.1.2.4 Functionality of the HMI No requirements are specified concerning the interpretation of the HMI.

 The following Datapoints shall allow coping with various HMI flavours and approaches towards controlling switching actuators.

 1. Input IOO

 2. Parameter Enable Toggle Mode

 3. Parameter On Off Action

##### 1.1.3 Constraints
###### This FB does not foresee any functionality for scene controlling. The inputs in the switching actuator for scene control can be controlled by a dedicated FB for scene purposes.

###### 1.1.7.2 Input Info On Off

DP Name: Info On Off IOO Mandatory
FB Name: Light Switching Sensor Basic (LSSB) Can be internal
Description
The input „Info On Off” shall be used to receive the status of the switching actuator.
This information can be used solely for visualisation purposes, for realising the toggle functionality or
other purposes.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Switch
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.001
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
b Indicates the status of the switching actuator. M {0, 1} - Access Type
 Input
N  this 1  this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out:
Request Polling: Period:
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Actual value:
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
Exception Handling
If this DP is not received (communication failure or configuration mistake) and the toggle functionality is
implemented, then the specification the output SOO will still toggle, as specified in 1.1.2.3.
Special Features
None.

###### 1.1.7.3 Parameter On Off Action

FB: Light Switching Sensor Property Name On Off Action (OOA) Mandatory
Basic (LSSB) (Server): Optional

Description:
If this parameter is implemented, then SOO shall always send one single value (Off or On).
This parameter only makes sense in certain realisation flavours of this FB: see 1.1.2.2.
DPT: Name DPT_Switch DPT ID 1.001 Datatype format B1
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
b 0 = Off M {0,1} None None

SOO shall only send value ‘0’
1 = On

SOO shall only send value ‘1’

Communication:
DP Address: object_type: 421 PID: 51
(in the server) start_index: 1 nr_of_elem: 1

Property access: Read only Read/Write
Protection Read level - Write level Exception Handling: Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
Special Features:
None.

#### 1.2 FB Dimming Sensor Basic (Object Type 420)

##### 1.2.1 Aims and objectives
###### The FB Dimming Sensor Basic is used in the Application Domain Lighting for providing input data to dimming actuators. It specifies the functionality, for example contained in a switch or a push button, to increase or decrease the brightness of a lamp or to switch the lamp on/off.

 Display elements (with own FBs) can be integrated to show the status of the dimming actuator.

 The inputs and outputs of the Functional Block are described but not the Human Machine Interface (HMI). Consequently, the manufacturers of the button or switch have the opportunity to implement their design and their operation methods.

##### 1.2.2 Functional specification

###### 1.2.2.1 Overview The FB Dimming Sensor Basic provides hardwired inputs for triggering transmission of values of output Datapoints.

FB Dimming Sensor FB Dimming Actuator

IOO SOO SOO IOO

RSC RSC

###### Figure 8 – Basic communication model (example with Relative Dimming Sensor)

 Figure 8 gives an application example in which the lighting is controlled relatively: the set value of the dimmer is increased and decreased in relative steps starting from the current value. It is also possible to control the set value of the FB Dimming Actuator directly through the DP Absolute Setvalue Control (ASC), as shown in Figure 9. Both models can be combined in a sensor implementation.

 1.2.2.2 Parameter On Off Action The parameter On Off Action shall limit the values transmitted by the outputs SOO and RSC to either only 0 (“Off”) and “Dimming Down/Stop” or 1 (“On”) and “Dimming Up/Stop”.

 This mainly makes sense if an appliance is realised as a combination of two FBs DSB each with one interaction point. This realisation however is only meaningful if the parameter ETM is not implemented or is set to the value “Disable”.

 1.2.2.3 Toggle Mode Toggle Mode denotes the behaviour where the value of the output SOO inverts on each transmission. The value of SOO can be calculated by the device internally or by interpreting the received value of the input InfoOnOff (IOO).

 The concept of toggle mode is only meaningful in the realisation as given in Figure 11. In case the parameter Enable Toggle Mode (ETM) is set to the value Enable, the parameter On Off Action (OOA) becomes meaningless.

###### Figure 12 – Toggle Mode without IOO Figure 13 – Toggle Mode with IOO


###### Rule 1

 Each subsequent transmission on the DP SOO will have an inverted value compared to the previous transmission.

 SOOn+1 = NOT(SOOn)


###### Rule 2

 Rule 1 is in this case extended with the following: on each reception of IOO, SOO becomes the value of IOO.

 SOO = IOO


###### The relation between IOO and Toggle Mode (Figure 13) can be summarized in the following pseudo code.

if(Update(DP_IOO)) {// This is rule 2.
DP_SOO = GetValue(DP_IOO);
}
if (UserInteraction) { // This is rule 1.
DP_SOO = InvertValue(DP_SOO);
SendValue(DP_SOO);
}
###### The interpretation of Toggle Mode concerning DP RSC and DP ASC is manufacturer specific.

 1.2.2.4 Functionality of the HMI No requirements are specified concerning the interpretation of the HMI.

 The following parameters shall allow coping with various HMI flavours and approaches towards controlling dimming actuators.

 1. Input IOO

 2. Parameter Enable Toggle Mode

 3. Parameter On Off Action

##### 1.2.3 Constraints
###### This FB does not foresee any functionality for scene controlling. The inputs in the dimming actuator for scene control can be controlled by a dedicated FB for scene purposes.

 The step size for the DP Relative Setvalue Control is manufacturer specific. No standard parameter is foreseen to this purpose.

###### 1.2.7.2 Output Relative Setvalue Control

DP Name: Relative Setvalue Control
FB Name: Dimming Sensor Basic (DSB)
Description
This Output shall be used to increase or decrease the brightness (StepCode ≠ 0) of the dimming actuator
or to stop the ongoing dimming action (StepCode = 0).
According the requirements concerning the support of ranges by Output DPTs as specified in
Chapter 3/7/1 “Interworking Model” clauses 2.1.7.2.1.1 and 2.4 it is allowed that the range of the
StepCode be limited to values smaller than 111b. The value 000b shall however always be supported.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Control_Dimming
DPT Format: B1U3
Field Description
c Shall specify whether the dimming set
value shall be increased or decreased.

StepCode Shall specify the dimming step size.
Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus (only for output):
Exception Handling
Through the parameter On Off Action it is possible that on human interaction only one value of the range
of the field c is transmitted. This way, it can be configured that the sensor only dims up/stops the
dimming value or dims down/stops the dimming value.
Special Features

a) For allowed combinations of output Datapoints see Table 4

###### 1.2.7.3 Output Absolute Setvalue Control (ASC)

DP Name: Absolute Setvalue Control
FB Name: Dimming Sensor Basic (DSB)
Description
This output shall be used to directly set the setvalue of the dimming actuator.
The algorithm to calculate the value of this output is not standardised. It may be given through the
parameter Absolute Setvalue.
If the parameter On Off Action is implemented and has the value “Off”, then it is
output value only sends 0 %.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Scaling
DPT Format: U8
Field Description
UnsignedValue The set value for the dimming actuator.
Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:

Exception Handling
None.
Special Features
None.

###### 1.2.7.4 Input Info On Off

DP Name: Info On Off IOO Mandatory
FB Name: Dimming Sensor Basic (LSSB) Can be internal
Description
The input „Info On Off“ shall be used to receive the switching status of the dimming actuator.
This information can be used solely for visualisation purposes, for realising the toggle functionality or
other purposes.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Switch
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.001
Field Description Supp. Range Unit Default
b Indicates the status of the dimming actuator M {0, 1} - 0 = dimming actuator off
1 = dimming actuator on

Access Type
 Input
N  this 1  this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out:
Request Polling: Period:
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Actual value:
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
Exception Handling
If this DP is not received (communication failure or configuration mistake) and the toggle functionality is
implemented, then the specification the output SOO will still toggle, as specified in 1.2.2.3.
Special Features
None.

###### 1.2.7.5 Parameter On Off Action

FB: Dimming Sensor Basic Property Name On Off Action (OOA) Mandatory
(LSSB) (Server): Optional

Description:
If this parameter is implemented, then SOO and RSC shall always send one single value (Off respectively
Dimming Down/Stop or On respectively Dimming Up/Stop).
This parameter only makes sense in certain realisation flavours of this FB: see 1.2.2.2.
The influence of this Parameter on the Output ASC is not standardised.
DPT: Name DPT_Switch DPT ID 1.001 Datatype format B1
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
b 0 = Off M {0,1} None None

SOO shall only send value ‘0’
RSC shall only send value ‘dimming
down/stop’
1 = On

SOO shall only send value ‘1’
RSC shall only send value ‘dimming up/stop’

Communication:
DP Address: object_type: 420 PID: 51
(in the server) start_index: 1 nr_of_elem: 1

Property access: Read only Read/Write
Protection Read level - Write level Exception Handling: Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
Special Features:
None.

###### 1.2.7.6 Parameter Enable Toggle Mode

FB: Dimming Sensor Basic Property Name Enable Toggle Mode (ETM) Mandatory
(LSSB) (Server): Optional

Description:
If this parameter has the value “Enable” then the value of the output SOO shall toggle each time it is
transmitted; if this parameter has the value “Disable” then the output SOO shall not be toggled.
See 1.2.2.3.
DPT: Name DPT_Enable DPT ID 1.003 Datatype format B1
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
b Enables or disables Toggle Mode. M {0,1} None None
Communication:
DP Address: object_type: 420 PID: 52
(in the server) start_index: 1 nr_of_elem: 1

Property access: Read only Read/Write
Protection Read level - Write level Exception Handling: Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
Special Features:
None.

#### 1.3 FB Colour Temperature Setting Sensor (Object Type 426)

##### 1.3.1 Aims and objectives
###### The control of the colour of white light, named ‘tunable white’, considers the possibility to generate light quality for different human expectations respective to “biological light” for better good health.

##### 1.3.2 Introduction and overview
###### The FB Colour Temperature Setting Sensor is used in the Application Domain Lighting for providing input data to colour temperature actuators. It specifies the functionality, for example contained in a switch or a push button, to increase or decrease the colour temperature of a lamp.

 The implementation of this functionality is not restricted to push buttons only. It may for instance be implemented in a larger controller, scheduler, gateway…

###### The colour temperature is defined as absolute temperature (in Kelvin) of a black body. This black body changes its colour from “red” through “yellow” to “white” as its temperature increases (black body line – BBL).

 Figure 16 - Control of colour temperature along the BBL (black body line)

 The total output light intensity depends on the requested colour temperature and the brightness.

 Many light sources do not emit a light colour caused by the temperature of the light source itself and do not follow exactly the black body line (BBL).

EXAMPLE 1 LED or fluorescent lamp versus tungsten lamp.
###### The colour emitted from the light source that is perceived by the human eye and that matches closest to black body line is called Correlated Colour Temperature (CCT).

 In the context of Colour Temperature “TC” refers to the colour closest to the BBL aligned to tint line (Figure 16).

 The colour temperature range covers the area from “cold” blue colour (20 000 K) to warm red colour (1 000 K).

 Figure 17 - Colour Temperature range

 Display elements (with own FBs) can be integrated to show the status of the colour temperature actuator.

 The Inputs and Outputs of the Functional Block are described, but not the Human Machine Interface (HMI). Consequently, the manufacturers of the button or switch have the opportunity to implement their design and their operation methods.

 1.3.3.2 Functionality of the HMI No requirements are specified concerning the interpretation of the HMI.

##### 1.3.4 Constraints

######  This FB does not foresee any functionality for scene controlling. The inputs in the colour temperature
 actuator for scene control can be controlled by a dedicated FB for scene purposes.

  The step sizes for the DP Relative Setvalue Control and for DP Relative Brightness / Colour
 Temperature Control is manufacturer specific. No standard parameter is foreseen to this purpose.

###### 1.3.8.2 Output Absolute Colour Temperature Control (ACTC)

DP Name: Absolute Colour Temperature Abbr.: ACTC
Control

FB Name: Colour Temperature Setting Sensor (CTSS)
Description
This Output shall be used to directly set the colour temperature value of a lamp.
The algorithm to calculate the value of this output is not standardised. It may be given through the
parameter Absolute Colour Temperature Control Value.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Absolute_Colour_Temperature
DPT Format: U16 DPT_ID:
Field Description Supp.
Absolute Colour The colour temperature for the lamp. M
Temperature

Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics

Saved value:

###### 1.3.8.3 Output Relative Brightness Relative Colour Temperature (RBRCT)

DP Name: Relative Brightness Relative Colour Abbr.: RBRCT Mandatory
Temperature

FB Name: Colour Temperature Setting Sensor (CTSS) Can be internal
Description
This Output shall be used to simultaneously control the brightness and the colour temperature
(StepCodes ≠ 0) of the lamp or to stop the ongoing change (StepCodes = 0) of the brightness or the
colour temperature.
According the requirements concerning the support of ranges by Output DPTs as specified in
Chapter 3/7/1 “Interworking Model” clauses 2.1.7.2.1.1 and 2.4 it is allowed that the ranges of the
StepCodes be limited to values smaller than 111b. The values 000b shall however always be supported.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Brightness_Colour_Temperature_Control
DPT Format: r4B1U3r4B1U3B8 DPT_ID: 250.600
Field Description Supp. Range
cCT Shall specify whether the colour M {0,1}
temperature value shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the step size or the code to M implementation
Colour stop the change. specific. 000b
Temperature shall be

supported.

cB Shall specify whether the brightness value M {0,1}
shall be increased or decreased.

Step Code The amount of intervals in which the M implementation
Brightness range of 0 % to 100 % is subdivided, or specific. 000b

the break indication. shall be

supported.

Masks: b1 This field shall indicate whether the fields M {0,1}
cCT and Step Code Colour Temperature
are valid or not.

Masks: b0 This field shall indicate whether the fields M {0,1}
cB and Step Code Brightness are valid or
not.

###### 1.3.8.4 Output Brightness Colour Temperature Transition (BCTT)

DP Name: Brightness Colour Temperature Abbr.: BCTT
Transition

FB Name: Colour Temperature Setting Sensor (CTSS)
Description
This Output shall be used to control the transition for the brightness and for the colour temperature of the
lamp.
The algorithm to calculate the values of this output is not standardised. It may be given through the
parameter Absolute Colour Temperature Control Value.
In the FB Colour Temperature Setting Sensor, there is no standard Parameter for the
_Brightness in this DP: this shall be inherited from the Parameter Absolute Setvalue_
_Sensor Basic._
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Brightness_Colour_Temperature_Transition
DPT Format: U16U16U8B8 DPT_ID:
Field Description Supp.
Time Period Unsigned time value for calculating M 0 s to 6553,5 s
transition time.

Absolute Colour The colour temperature for the lamp. M
Temperature

Absolute The absolute brightness value for the M 0 % to 100 %
Brightness lamp.

Masks b2 b2: validity of the Time Period M {0,1}

Masks b1 b1: validity of the Absolute Colour M {0,1}
Temperature

Masks b0 b0: validity of the absolute brightness M {0,1}

###### 1.3.8.5 Input Current Colour Temperature (CCT)

DP Name: Current Colour Temperature CCT Mandatory
FB Name: Colour Temperature Setting Sensor (CTSS) Can be internal
Description
The Input “Current Colour Temperature” shall be used to receive the Current Colour Temperature from
the colour temperature actuator.
This information can be used solely for visualisation or other purposes.
NOTE 1 This Input does not give any indication whether the colour temperature actuator is switched on or off.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Absolute_Colour_Temperature
DPT Format: U16 DPT_ID: 7.600
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
Absolute The Current Colour Temperature of the colour M 0 K to K
Colour temperature actuator. 65 535 K
Temperature

Access Type

Value (ACT_CV)

This parameter shall define the value that shall be sent with the Outputs Absolute Colour Temperature
Control (ACTC) and Brightness Colour Temperature Transition (BCTT).
DPT: Name DPT_Absolute_Colour_Temperature DPT ID 7.600 Datatype format
Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
Absolute Colour Contains the value for ACTC and M 0 K to K None.
Temperature BCTT. 65 535 K

#### 1.4 FB Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (Object Type 424)

##### 1.4.1 Aims and objectives
###### The control of the RGB Colour Setting considered the possibility to generate simple Colour Setting control, mostly for residential applications (e.g. RGB luminaire in a bathroom) or for other applications where non colour referenced luminaires are sufficient.

 1.4.1.1 Introduction and overview The FB Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) is used in the Application Domain Lighting for providing input data to a colour actuator. It specifies the functionality, for example contained in a room control unit (e.g. with display for change of the colour with dedicated user interaction), to modify the colour of a lamp.

 The implementation of this functionality is not restricted to push buttons only. It may for instance be implemented in a larger controller, scheduler, gateway …

###### Respective to different colour coding models the FB shall at least support the two following models:
  RGB(W) Other encodings and models may additionally be supported.

##### 1.4.2 Definitions
###### Primary light output  The colour of each primary light emitted by the lamp connected to the implementation of the FB CARGB.

 Possible primaries are “red”, “green”, “blue” and “white”

 light output brightness The brightness of the light emitted by the lamp connected to the implementation of the FB CARGB.

 Primary set value The internal set value of the each primary light output 

 Combined light output This is the colour resulting from the combination of the Primaries. 

 This model has the following restrictions.
  The whole range of human colour perception is quite large. Not all possible colours can be
 represented. It may for instance require negative components to represent certain colours.  Different colour reproducing devices have different “red”, “green”, “blue” primaries. The realised
 colour in the RGB colour model is device-dependent. Summary for the use of the RGB colour model

  This is useful for simple colour control.  Because of the device dependent interpretation of RGB, this coding is only suitable for
 point-to-point communication, this is, if there is only a single receiver.

 1.4.2.1 Various Display elements (with own FBs) can be integrated to show the status of the colour control actuator.

 The Inputs and Outputs of the Functional Block are described, but not the Human Machine Interface (HMI). Consequently, the manufacturers of the colour control sensor devices have the opportunity to implement their design and their operation methods.

##### 1.4.3 Functional specification

###### 1.4.3.1 Overview The FB Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) provides hardwired inputs for triggering transmission of values of output Datapoints.

##### 1.4.4 Constraints
###### This FB does not foresee any functionality for scene controlling. The Inputs in the colour control actuator for scene control can be controlled by a dedicated FB for scene purposes.

 The step sizes for the DP Colour_RC_RGB and DP Colour_RC_RGBW is manufacturer specific. No standard parameter is foreseen to this purpose.

###### 1.4.9.1 Output Colour Set RGB (CS_RGB)

DP Name: Colour Set RGB
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (CSSRGB)
Description
This Output shall be used to Control the RGB colour of the colour actuator.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Colour_RGB
DPT Format: U8U8U8
Field Description
R This shall be the part of red in the colour
set value.

G This shall be the part of green in the
colour set value.

B This shall be the part of blue in the colour
set value.

Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus (only for output):
Exception Handling
The used DPT does not allow indicating either field as invalid or don’t care. It is not possible to control
only one or two colour primitives and leave the two or one remaining colour primitives unchanged. All
fields in the used DPT are always valid.
If one of the colour components is not valid, the information cannot be transmitted with this Datapoint
(value=0 means: the colour component is switched off, but valid).
Special Features

Because of the device dependent interpretation of RGB, this Datapoint is more suited for point-to-point
communication, this is, if there is only a single receiver, than for point-to-multipoint communication.

###### 1.4.9.2 Output Colour_Relative Control_RGB (RC_RGB)

DP Name: Colour Relative Control RGB Abbr.:
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (CSSRGB)
Description
This Output shall be used to relatively increment and decrement (StepCodes ≠ 0) the contribution of
each colour component (StepCodes ≠ 0) of the colour actuator or to stop the ongoing change
(StepCodes = 0).
According the requirements concerning the support of ranges by Output DPTs as specified in
Chapter 3/7/1 “Interworking Model” clauses 2.1.7.2.1.1 and 2.4 it is allowed that the ranges of the
StepCodes be limited to values smaller than 111b. The values 000b shall however always be supported.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Relative_Control_RGB
DPT Format: B1U3B1U3B1U3
Field Description Supp.
cR Shall specify whether the colour M
component red shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M
Colour Red code to stop the fading of the colour red.

cG Shall specify whether the colour M
component green shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M
Colour code to stop the fading of the colour
Green green.

cB Shall specify whether the colour M
component blue shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M
Colour Blue code to stop the fading of the colour blue.

Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus (only for output):
Exception Handling
None.
Special Features
None.

a) For allowed combinations of output Datapoints see Table 9.

###### 1.4.9.3 Output Colour Set RGBW (CS_RGBW)

DP Name: Colour Set RGBW
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (CSSRGB)
Description
This Output shall be used to Control the RGBW colour of the colour actuator.
NOTE 2
DPT_Colour_RGBW used in this DP foresees mask bits for each colour component. This makes that a sensor can
control any colour component separately without influencing the other colour components.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Colour_RGBW
DPT Format: U8U8U8U8r8r4B4
Field Description
R Colour Level Red
G Colour Level Green
B Colour Level Blue
W Colour Level White
mR Shall specify whether the colour information red
in the field R is valid or not.

mG Shall specify whether the colour information
green in the field G is valid or not.

mB Shall specify whether the colour information blue
in the field B is valid or not.

mW Shall specify whether the colour information
white in the field W is valid or not.

Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus (only for output):
Exception Handling
None.
Special Features

Because of the device dependent interpretation of RGB, this Datapoint is more suited for point-to-point
communication, this is, if there is only a single receiver, than for point-to-multipoint communication.

a) For allowed combinations of output Datapoints see Table 9.

###### 1.4.9.4 Output Colour Relative Control RGBW (RC_RGBW)

DP Name: Colour Relative Control RGBW Abbr.: RC_RGBW Mandatory
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (CSSRGB) Can be internal
Description
This Output shall be used to relatively increment and decrement (StepCodes ≠ 0) the contribution of
each colour component (StepCodes ≠ 0) of the colour actuator or to stop the ongoing change
(StepCodes = 0).
According the requirements concerning the support of ranges by Output DPTs as specified in
Chapter 3/7/1 “Interworking Model” clauses 2.1.7.2.1.1 and 2.4 it is allowed that the ranges of the
StepCodes be limited to values smaller than 111b. The values 000b shall however always be supported.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Relative_Control_RGBW
DPT Format: r4B1U3r4B1U3r4B1U3r4B1U3B8 DPT_ID: 252.600
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
cR Shall specify whether the colour M {0,1} None.
component red shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M 000b to 111b None.
Colour Red code to stop the fading of the colour red

cG Shall specify whether the colour M {0,1} None.
component gree shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M 000b to 111b None.
Colour code to stop the fading of the colour green
Green

cB Shall specify whether the colour M {0,1} None.
component blue shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M 000b to 111b None.
Colour Blue code to stop the fading of the colour blue

cW Shall specify whether the colour M {0,1} None.
component blue shall be increased or
decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the M 000b to 111b None.
Colour White code to stop the fading of the colour white

Masks: b3 This field shall indicate the validity of the M {0,1} None.
fields CR and Step Code Colour Red.

Masks: b2 This field shall indicate the validity of the M {0,1} None.
fields CG and Step Code Colour Green.

Masks: b1 This field shall indicate the validity of the M {0,1} None.
fields CB and Step Code Colour Blue.

Masks: b0 This field shall indicate the validity of the M {0,1} None.
fields CW and Step Code Colour White.

###### 1.4.9.5 Input Current Colour RGB (CC_RGB)

DP Name: Actual Colour_RGB (CC_RGB) CC_RGB Mandatory
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (CSSRGB) Can be internal
Description
This Input shall be used to receive the RGB colour of the colour actuator.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Colour_RGB
DPT Format: U8U8U8 DPT_ID: 232.600
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
R This shall be the part of red in the colour set M 0 to 255 none
value.

G This shall be the part of green in the colour set M 0 to 255 none
value.

B This shall be the part of blue in the colour set M 0 to 255 none
value.

Access Type
 Input
N  this 1  this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out:
Request Polling: Period:
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Actual value:
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
Exception Handling
If one of the colour components is not valid, the information cannot be transmitted with this datapoint
(value=0 means: the colour component is switched off, but valid)
Special Features
None.

###### 1.4.9.6 Input Current Colour RGBW (CC_RGBW)

DP Name: Actual Colour_RGBW (CC_RGBW) CC_RGBW Mandatory
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor RGB(W) (CSSRGB) Can be internal
Description
This Input shall be used to receive the RGBW colour of the colour actuator.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Colour_RGBW
DPT Format: U8U8U8U8r8r4B4 DPT_ID: 251.600
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
R Colour Level Red M 0-255 G Colour Level Green M 0-255 B Colour Level Blue M 0-255 W Colour Level White M 0-255 mR Shall specify whether the colour information red in M {0,1} the field R is valid or not.

mG Shall specify whether the colour information green M {0,1} in the field G is valid or not.

mB Shall specify whether the colour information blue M {0,1} in the field B is valid or not.

mW Shall specify whether the colour information white M {0,1} in the field W is valid or not.

Access Type
 Input

###### 1.4.9.7 Parameter Absolute RGB Colour Control Value (RGB_CCV)

FB: Colour Setting Sensor Property Name (Server): Absolute_ Mandatory
RGB(W) (CSSRGB) RGB_Control_ Optional

Value
(RGB_CCV)

Description:
This parameter shall define the value that shall be sent with the output Colour Set RGB (CS_RGB).
DPT: Name DPT_Colour_- DPT ID 232.600 Datatype format U8U8U8
RGB

Field Description Sup. Range Unit Default
R This shall be the part of red in M 0 to 255 none none
the colour set value.

G This shall be the part of green in M 0 to 255 none none
the colour set value.

B This shall be the part of blue in M 0 to 255 none none
the colour set value.

Communication:
DP Address: object_type: 424 PID: 101
(in the server) start_index: 1 nr_of_elem: 1

Property access: Read only Read/Write
Protection Read level - Write level Exception Handling: Value after Power-up: Stored Value Act Value Default Value
None.
Special Features:
None.

#### 1.5 FB Colour Setting Sensor xyY (Object Type 425)

##### 1.5.1 Aims and objectives

###### 1.5.1.1 General The control of the xyY colour considers the possibility to generate professional colour control, mostly for  commercial applications (e.g. in a museum, shops for meat, vegetables, fruit …) or for other applications where exact colour referenced luminaires are necessary.

 1.5.1.2 Introduction and overview The FB Colour Setting Sensor xyY is used in the Application Domain Lighting for providing input data to a colour actuator. It specifies the functionality, for example contained in a room control unit (e.g. with display for change of the colour with dedicated user interaction), to modify the colour of a lamp.

 The implementation of this functionality is not restricted to push buttons only. It may for instance be implemented in a larger controller, scheduler, gateway …

###### Figure 26 – Overview of the Application Model Colour Control in the Application Domain Lighting

 Respective to different colour coding models the FB shall at least support the following model:
  xyY Other encodings and models may additionally be supported.


-----

###### 1.5.1.3 Colour model xyY The colour triangle is a plane figure scaled in such a way that any colour within it may be identified with two coordinates x and y, where x and y are both in a range 0 to 1. The total output light intensity depends on the requested xy-coordinate and the brightness (luminance) Y.

 Figure 27 - Control of colour with Colour Type xyY

 Third dimension: brightness or luminance (indicated by Y).

 Figure 28 – xyY diagram

 Using the xyY values, any two colours can be compared to determine whether they match. This is the whole purpose of CIE's standards.

 Summary for the use of xyY control

 It is useful for the more professional applications. As this interpretation is device independent, it is better suited in communication models with multiple receivers.

 For colour control within the xyY-Colour Model, it shall optionally be possible to control the colour relative.

EXAMPLE 2 Curve A shows the change of colour while the saturation is kept constant (distance to the White Point
WP)
EXAMPLE 3 Curve B shows the change of saturation (distance to the White Point) while the colour is kept
constant
EXAMPLE 4 Curve C shows the simultaneous change of saturation and colour
EXAMPLE 5 Not shown here is the simultaneous change of Brightness.

 1.5.1.4 Various Display elements (with own FBs) can be integrated to show the status of the colour control actuator.

 The Inputs and Outputs of the Functional Block are described, but not the Human Machine Interface (HMI). Consequently, the manufacturers of the colour control sensor devices have the opportunity to implement their design and their operation methods.

##### 1.5.3 Constraints
###### This FB does not foresee any functionality for scene controlling. The Inputs in the colour control actuator for scene control can be controlled by a dedicated FB for scene purposes.

 The step sizes for the DP Colour_RC_RGB and DP Colour_RC_RGBW are implementation specific. No standard parameter is foreseen to this purpose.

Input Current Colour xyY _O_ _(GO)_ _(GO)_
Output Colour Set xyY _O_ _GO_ _GO_
Output Colour_RC_xyY _O_ _(GO)_ _(GO)_
Output Colour_Transition_xyY _O_ _(GO)_ _(GO)_

###### CSSxyY FB Profile 1 models the Colour Setting Sensor xyY without any additional Inputs or Outputs. This is the minimal requirement.

 This can optionally be extended with the Outputs for relative xyY colour control (Output Colour_RC_xyY) and xyY colour transition (Output Colour_Transition_xyY). Further, the Input Current Colour xyY may be added.

 In case of Profile 1 it may also be possible to optionally integrate (beside DP Colour_RC_xyY) in addition three separate, additional Datapoints according DPT_Control_Dimming(3.007) for separate relative control of the xyY-colour (one Datapoint for relative control of brightness, one Datapoint for relative control of colour and one Datapoint for relative control of saturation).

 Table 12 - Parameters

Parameters XYY_CCV O O
XYY_CCTT O O

###### As regards the implementation of Parameters in Standard Mode or the LTE-Mode Standard Mode Interface, in case of memory mapped Datapoints the DPT may be implementation specific. In case of implementation as a Property of an Interface Object, the use of the standardised parameter specification is mandatory. 

5) Please refer to [02] for the definition of the syntax and symbols used in this FB Profile definition.

###### 1.5.7.2 Output Colour_Relative Control_xyY (RC_xyY)

DP Name: Colour Relative Control xyY Abbr.:
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor xyY (CSSXYY)
Description
This Output shall be used to simultaneous increase or decrease the brightness, the colour and the
saturation (StepCodes ≠ 0) of the colour actuator or to stop the ongoing change (StepCodes = 0).
According the requirements concerning the support of ranges by Output DPTs as specified in
Chapter 3/7/1 “Interworking Model” clauses 2.1.7.2.1.1 and 2.4 it is allowed that the ranges of the
StepCodes be limited to values smaller than 111b. The values 000b shall however always be supported.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Relative_Control_xyY
DPT Format: r4B1U3r4B1U3r4B1U3B8
Field Description
cS Shall specify whether the saturation of the
colour shall be increased or decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the
Saturation code to stop the fading of the saturation

cC Shall specify whether the colour shall be
increased or decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the
Colour code to stop the fading of the colour

cB Shall specify whether the brightness shall
be increased or decreased.

Step Code Shall specify the fading step size or to the
Brightness code to stop the fading of the brightness

Masks: b2 This field shall indicate whether the fields cS
and Step Code Saturation are valid or not.

Masks: b1 This field shall indicate whether the fields cC
and Step Code Colour are valid or not.

Masks: b0 This field shall indicate whether the fields cB
and Step Code Brightness are valid or not.

Access Type
 Output

###### 1.5.7.3 Output Colour_Transition_xyY (CT_xyY) 

DP Name: Colour_Transition_xyY Abbr.:
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor xyY (CSSXYY)
Description
This Output shall be used to Control the transition for the xyY colour of the colour actuator.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Colour_Transition_xyY
DPT Format: U16U16U16U8r6B2
Field Description
Time Period Unsigned time-value for calculating
fading time.

x-axis x-coordinate of the colour information
y-axis y-coordinate of the colour information
Brightness Brightness of the colour
C This field shall indicate whether the
colour information in the fields x-axis
and y-axis is valid or not.

B This field shall indicate whether the
brightness information in the field
_Brightness is valid or not._

Access Type
 Output
this  M this  1
Spontaneous COV: Δ-Value:
Cyclic Period:
Request
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint
Default Group Address: --Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation:
Saved value:
Transmit on bus (only for output):
Exception Handling
None.
Special Features
None.

a) For allowed combinations of output Datapoints see 1.5.6.

###### 1.5.7.4 Input Current Colour xyY (CC_xyY)

DP Name: Current Colour_xyY CC_xyY Mandatory
FB Name: Colour Setting Sensor xyY (CSSXYY) Can be internal
Description
This Input shall be used to receive the xyY colour of the colour actuator.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Colour_xyY
DPT Format: U16U16U8r6B2 DPT_ID: 242.600
Field Description Supp. Range Unit
x-axis x-coordinate of the colour information M 0 to65 535 None.
y-axis y-coordinate of the colour information M 0 to65 535 None.
Brightness Brightness of the colour M 0 % to 100 % None.
C This field shall indicate whether the colour M {0,1} None.
information in the fields x-axis and y-axis is
valid or not.

B This field shall indicate whether the M {0,1} None.
brightness information in the field
_Brightness is valid or not._

### 2 FB Movement Detector for Lighting

#### 2.1 Aims and objectives
###### The “Movement Detector for Lighting“ (FB MDL) shall control actuators for lighting in function of:
 - the detection of movement, and - the detected brightness.

 The brightness information may be retrieved either from a hardwired input, or from the Input Brightness External, e.g. provided by the FB Room Light Sensor.

 The dependency of the functionality on this brightness is the basic difference between this FB MDL and similar FBs for HVAC and for Anti-Intrusion.

NOTE 3 This FB Movement Detector for Lighting is primarily designed for use in the application domain Lighting. Its 1 bit Outputs
however allow this FB to be used in other application domains as well. Further integration in other application domains is possible
through generic FBs, as FB Scene Control. See 2.2.11.

#### 2.2 Functional specification

##### 2.2.1 Basic functionality
###### The FB MDL shall be able to detect movement in a physical movement sensor, typically PIR (Passive InfrRed), and to transmit this information on the bus via at least one Output Switch On Off (SOO) or Timed StartStop (TSS).

 The FB MDL may have further Inputs and functionality.
 1. Input Movement Trigger shall serve for receiving movement signals from an external movement detector. 2. Input Info OnOff shall serve to suppress the faulty detection of movement at the moment that the light is switched. 3. The brightness evaluation shall serve for surpressing light switching if the brightness in the detection area is above a certain threshold level.

 The combination and sequence of these functions is not specified. Further on in this specification multiple use cases are specified. The choice for the design of the realisation of this FB MDL depends on the main use case that is intended to be solved.

 Figure 33 gives a possible design; alternative solutions are possible as well.

##### 2.2.2 Physical means to detect movement
###### The FB MDL shall have a physical movement sensor to be able to detect movement. This can be done through the use of various physical means, such as PIR, microwaves … These physical means may also be combined. These means are however not modelled differently in this KNX FB MDL. All movement detectors for lighting are modelled through this one single common FB MDL without taking the physical detection method into consideration any further.

 A first timer in the FB MDL shall be the Movement Signal Lowpass Timer (MSLT).

 Timer MSLT is started and retriggered on any physical detection of movement. A running timer MSLT thus signals that the device has detected a valid movement signal.

 Timer MSLT is the timer that shall prevent that if movement is detected with a higher frequency (e.g. multiple detections during 1 second) that this leads to as many transmissions on the bus.

 The timer MSLT depends on the applied hardware, electronics, etc. and is product specific. Therefore, the timer MSLT is not available as an application parameter.

 The state of the MSLT timer shall be the output signal of this physical movement sensor.

##### 2.2.3 Outputs Switch OnOff and Timed StartStop
###### These Outputs reflect two typical use cases of this FB MDL.

##### 2.2.4 Time dependencies

###### 2.2.4.1 Timer definitions Next to the above specified timer MSLT, FB MDL shall have a further timer. This second timer shall be the Output Control Timer (OCT). Timer OCT shall be the timer that shall control

 - the transmission of SOO, or
 - the periodic transmission of TSS.

 The time-out value of OCT is available as application parameter.

EXAMPLE 6 Timer MSLT is 5 s to 10 s; Timer OCT is 45 s.

###### 2.2.4.2 For Timed StartStop Timer MSLT shall be started on the first detection of movement. It shall be retriggered on every renewed detection of movement.

 Timer OCT shall be started when Timer MSLT is started. When Timer OCT expires and Timer MSLT is running, then Timer OCT shall be automatically restarted. Timer OCT is never retriggered and never stopped.

 Output TSS shall transmit the value Start when Timer OCT is started or restarted. The Output TSS shall in this case never transmit the value Stop.

 2.2.4.3 For Switch OnOff Timer MSLT shall be started on the first detection of movement. It shall be retriggered on every renewed detection of motion.

 Timer OCT shall be reset and started if Timer MSLT expires. Timer OCT is stopped if Timer MSLT is started.

 Output SOO shall transmit the value On when Timer MSLT is started and Timer OCT is not running.

 Output SOO shall transmit the value Off if Timer OCT expires. It is not transmitted if Timer MSLT expires or if Timer OCT is stopped.

##### 2.2.5 Brightness dependency
###### The functionality of the FB MDL shall further be influenced by the current brightness.

USE CASE 3 If movement is detected, the FB MDL will switch on the light if the brightness is below the threshold. The
measured brightness will by this increase. Yet, this FB MDL should again switch off the light when it no longer detects any
movement. This means that while OCT runs, the FB MDL works independently of the measured brightness.

###### If a first movement is detected, the FB MDL will switch on the light, via SOO or TSS. If further movement is detected, SOO may and TSS shall be repeated. If no more movement is detected then SOO shall transmit the value Off. This means that the brightness is only evaluated for the initial movement detection when the timers MSLT and OCT are started.

###### 1. The initial reaction of the FB MDL, this is, on the first detection of movement, when both timers are expired, shall be as specified in Table 14.

 Table 14 – INITIAL reaction of FB MDL

 2. When either one of the timers Timer MSLT or Timer OCT is running, the functionality of the FB MDL shall be independent of the measured brightness and shall be as specified in 2.2.4.

 The Parameter Enable Brightness Independency (EBI) shall be used to control this brightness dependency. If EBI is not implemented, then the FB MDL shall always operate brightness dependent concerning the initial detection of movement.

 The threshold value may optionally be controlled through the Parameter Brightness Threshold as specified in 2.7.7.

 The current brightness is typically obtained from a built-in brightness sensor. It may as well (additionally) be received through the Input Brightness External. In case a build-in brightness sensor is combined with one or more external brightness sensors, the relation between both is implementation dependent.

##### 2.2.6 Input Info OnOff and Parameter Movement Sensor Pause Time
###### The Input “Info OnOff” shall be used to receive the status of an actuator.

 This shall allow the FB MDL to know the moment when a light is switched, off or on, to suppress a movement detection from the light source.

 On reception any value, On or Off, on the Input Info OnOff, the FB MDL shall not evaluate the physical movement signals for a short time. This time can be fixed in the device or can be given by the parameter Movement Sensor Pause Time (MSPT). During this time the physical movement sensor signals shall not be evaluated. The implementation of this is not fixed; it may be implemented for instance as follows (informative).

 - On reception of a telegram on the Input Info OnOff, the FB MDL will start a timer, with a value according the parameter MSPT if implemented, during which the internal signal MSLT will not cause the transmission of SOO or TSS.

 - On detection of movement through the internal signal MSLT, a timer is started, with a value according the parameter MSPT if implemented. If any telegram is received on the Input IOO while this timer is running then there will be no transmission of SOO or TSS; if no telegram is received on the Input IOO, then SOO and TSS will be handled as normal.

 - Combinations of the above and alternative solutions can be considered as well.

EXAMPLE 7 3 s

###### This Input shall also allow to inhibit the evaluation of the internal signal MSLT state, as explained in USE CASE 6 and in the specification of the parameter Trigger continue in clause 2.2.9.

|Current brightness|SOO|TSS|
|---|---|---|
|**below threshold value**|Shall transmit On.|Shall transmit Start.|
|**above threshold value**|No action.|No action.|

##### 2.2.7 Input Enable
###### The Input Enable shall be used to limit the transmission of the Outputs TSS and SOO. The influence of this Input may be located at multiple possible locations inside the FB MDL. Depending on this, the effect of the Input Enable may be
 - to stop all communication of TSS and SOO, or - to stop only the evaluation of the internal movement sensor, or - to stop the evaluation of the external signal MT,

 or any combination of the above.

 Input Enable is however not intended to disable the brightness evaluation. To this, the Input Enable Brightness Independency shall be used (see 2.2.5).

USE CASE 4 This functionality can be used to disable the light switching by a movement detector at night e.g. without forcing
(Input Forced) an actuator.

USE CASE 5 During cleaning of the area that is covered by this movement detector, this Input allows preventing
that the light is switched on and off repeatedly.

##### 2.2.8 Input Movement Trigger
###### The Input Movement Trigger (MT) serves for connecting external movement detecting.

 The evaluation of the Input Movement Trigger (MT) is not fixed.

 1. It may be evaluated in the same way as the internal physical movement sensor signal (MSLT state) of the FB MDL. It then starts the timer OCT as specified in 2.2.4. The transmission of the Outputs TSS or SOO may be under the control of the Parameter Movement Trigger Evaluation (see 2.7.10).

USE CASE 6 If the light within a room is controlled through push buttons as well as through movement detectors, it
may be wanted that the light is switched on through a push button but is switched off automatically by the movement
detector. To allow this, the push button communicates through this Input with the FB MDL instead of directly with the
light actuator.

###### Figure 36 – USE CASE 6 – solution 1 FB MDL evaluates timers and brightness in the interpretation of MT

 - In the design of the FB MDL in this solution, the Input MT does not directly affect the Outputs, but is subject to the timer OCT. When this timer expires, it will switch off the light. This model guarantees that the light is always switched off, even if the FB MDL did not detect movement itself.

 - If the design of the FB MDL still evaluates the internal brightness sensor, it may occur that the request for switching on the light from the FB LSSB, is not passed by the FB MDL if the brightness is below the threshold value. The light is not switched on, even though it is requested by a person. This can be solved by the Parameter Movement Trigger Evaluation, which makes that the brightness is not evaluated for the Input MT.

 2. The Input MT may also be evaluated elsewhere in the functional scheme of the FB MDL (Figure 33). The Input MT can be implemented so that it directly controls the transmission of the Outputs SOO or TSS, without further evaluation of timers or the brightness. ##### 2.2.9 Trigger continue
###### If the Parameter Trigger Continue (TC) is set to Enable, then the motion detector shall be active only if the output of the actuator is really switched on. The FB MDL shall recognise this actuator state by its Input Info OnOff. The FB MDL then retriggers the actuator channel while cyclically sending the value On on the Output Switch OnOff.

 If the Parameter Trigger Continue is set to Disable then the FB MDL works independently from the Datapoint Info OnOff except the suppression of switching of the light.

##### 2.2.10 Master/slave relation between FB MDL

###### 2.2.10.1 Introduction If the lighting in a larger area is controlled by more than one movement detector, then it shall be avoided that one movement detector switches the light off, while another movement detector switches the light on. This may be solved by a master/slave concept between the movement detectors. One movement detector controls the lighting; the other movement detector(s) do not control the lighting but report their movement detection through their Outputs TSS to the master via the Input Movement Trigger of the master. The functionality of the master FB MDL is further unchanged, i.e. it is further controlled through its Inputs Enable, etc.

###### Figure 39 – Master-Slave Solution 1

USE CASE 7 It may happen that the FB MDL Master detects the first movement and switches the FB LSAB. It may then
however occur that FB MDL Master does not detect any further movement and would switch off FB LSAB after timer OCT in the
FB MDL Master expires, even if FB MDL Slave detects movement. This happens if the person has moved out of the detection area
of FB MDL Masters into the detection area of the FB MDL Slave. This requires that the FB MDL Slave operates independently of the
light brightness. This is done by linking the Output SOO of the FB MDL Master with the Input EBI of the FB MDL Slave.

USE CASE 8 If the FB MDL Slave detects the first movement and the brightness is below the threshold, it will trigger the
FB MDL Master, which shall take the final conclusion about switching the light, depending on its further parameters.
If the person moves from the detection area of the FB MDL Slave into the detection area of the FB MDL Master, then the FB MDL
Master detects its first movement: the OCT in the FB MDL Master is retriggered by the own movement detection in the FB MDL
Master and no longer from its Input MT. This is independent of the brightness detected by the FB MDL Master: with a running OCT,
the brightness is not evaluated (see 2.2.5).

###### Figure 40 – Master-Slave Solution 2

USE CASE 9 The FB MDL Master detects the first movement and switches the FB LSAB through its Output TSS.
If the person moves from the detection area of the FB MDL Master into the detection area of the FB MDL Slave then the
FB MDL Master will not detect any further movement and the LSAB switches off the light autonomously after its switch off
delay has expired, even if FB MDL Slave detects movement. This requires that the FB MDL Slave operates independently of
the light brightness. This is done by linking the Output TSS of the FB MDL Master with the Input MT of the FB MDL Slave.
This shall cause the timer MSLT in the FB MDL Slave to be started, which shall in turn cause that the FB MDL Slave operates
brightness independently. However, it shall be avoided that the FB MDL Slave transmits on its Output TSS back to MT of the
FB MDL Master: this will cause as many transmissions of TSS signals on the bus as there are FB MDL Slaves connected to
the master. This can be avoided by appropriate setting of the Parameter Movement Trigger Evaluation.

USE CASE 10 If the FB MDL Slave detects the first movement and the brightness is below the threshold, it will
trigger the FB MDL Master, which shall take the final conclusion about switching the light, depending on its further parameters.
If the person moves from the detection area of the FB MDL Slave into the detection area of the FB MDL Master, then the
FB MDL Master detects its first movement: the OCT in the FB MDL Master is retriggered by the own movement detection in
the FB MDL Master and no longer from its Input MT. This is independent of the brightness detected by the FB MDL Master:
with a running OCT, the brightness is not evaluated (see 2.2.5).

#### 2.3 Contraints
###### For evaluation of the illuminance from an external illuminance sensor, this FB MDL solely provides the Input Brightness External (BE), which may be compared to internal threshold values or an internal illuminance sensor. If the external illuminance sensor has an own evaluation of the illuminance and provides a 1 bit Output, then this can be linked to the Input Enable.

|**Outputs**|**Outputs**|**Outputs**|
|Switch OnOff|Switches on or off the light.|1.001 DPTSwitch|

|Datapoint|Description/Remarks|Datapoint Type|
|---|---|---|
|Enable|Enables and disables the detection of movement.|1.003 DPTEnable|
|Brightness External|Receives the external brightness level.|_<br>9.004 DPTValueLux|
|Movement Trigger|Add an external physical movement detector signal<br>to the FB.|__<br>1.010 DPT_Start|
|**Parameters**|**Parameters**|**Parameters**|
|Brightness Threshold|Threshold value above which the detection of<br>movement is disabled.|9.004 DPT_Value_Lux|
|Output Control Time|The time after that the movement detector will wait<br>for switching off the light after the last detection of<br>moevement (expiration of MSLT timer) via SOO, or<br>the time in-between transmissions of TSS if TSS is<br>repeated.|7.008 DPT_TimePeriodSec|
|Trigger Continue|Defines the dependency of the FB MDL from its<br>Input IOO.|1.003 DPT_Enable|
|Enable Brightness<br>Independency|Controls whether or not the functionality depends on<br>the received or measured brightness.|1.003 DPT_Enable|
|Movement Sensor Pause<br>Time|Short period after reception of the value on on the<br>Input IOO during which the detection of movement<br>shall be surpressed.|7.004<br>DPT_TimePeriod100Msec|
|Movement Trigger<br>Evaluation|Specifies the handling of the Input Movement<br>Trigger.|1.003 DPT_Enable|

##### 2.7.2 Output Time StartStop (TSS)

DP Name: Timed StartStop Abbr.: TSS Mandatory
FB Name: FB Movement Detector for Lighting (MDL) Can be internal
Description
Please refer to the functional specification.
This Output shall service for switching on the light. This can be used with a lighting actuator that switches
off the light autonomously, e.g. after a certain period.
This Output value shall be encoded according DPT_Start (1.010). Only the value 1 = start shall be
transmitted; the value 0 = stop shall not be transmitted.
As long as the FB MDL detects movement it shall send the value 1 = start periodically with the period
according the Parameter OCT.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Start
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.010
Field Supp. Range Unit Default
b This shall switch on the light. M {0} none 0

##### 2.7.3 Input Info OnOff (IOO)

DP Name: Info OnOff Abbr.: IOO Mandatory
FB Name: FB Movement Detector for Lighting (MDL) Can be internal
Description
Please refer to the functional specification.
When the light switches on or off in the spatial area in which the FB Movement Detector is physically
mounted, this may by the electronics erroneously be detected as a movement. To prevent from this, the
information to switch the light (e.g. from the light sensor) can be linked also to this Input Info OnOff. If the
FB MDL receives a telegram on this Input, it will for a short period, possibly according the parameter
Parameter Movement Sensor Pause Time2.7.11, not evaluate any movement sensor signal (internal
signals MSLT).
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Switch
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID:
Field Supp. Range Unit
b 0: The light is or will be switched off. M {0, 1} none
1: The light is or will be switched on.

##### 2.7.4 Input Enable (EN)

DP Name: Enable Abbr.: EN Mandatory
FB Name: FB Movement Detector for Lighting Can be internal
Description
Please refer to the functional specification.
This Input shall serve to limit the transmission of the Outputs SOO and/or TSS. The transmissions may
either be disabled totally, or be limited to transmissions only caused by the Input MT.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Enable
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.003
Field Supp. Range Unit
b 0 = disable M {0, 1} none

The transmissions of the Outputs SOO
and/or TSS are limited. The movement
signals that are caused by the built-in
movement detector shall be disabled. Other
conditions for the transmission of SOO
and/or TSS may still be evaluated[ a)].
1 = enable

The transmissions of the Ouputs SOO
and/or TSS shall not be limited by this Input.

Access Type
 Input
N  this 1  this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out:
Request Polling: Period:
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address:
Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
Exception Handling
a) It may happen that the FB MDL is disabled while the timer OCT is running. When OCT expires, it
may thus still happen that the FB MDL switches off the light. This is implementation dependent.
Special Features
None.

##### 2.7.5 Input Brightness External (BE)

DP Name: Brightness External Abbr.: BE Mandatory
FB Name: Movement Detector for Lighting Can be internal
Description
This Input shall allow for the reception of the current brightness provided by an external room light sensor.
This allows

 for a FB MDL without built-in brightness sensor, or
 for extra brightness information in addition to the brightness measured by the built-in brightness

sensor.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Value_Lux
DPT Format: F16 DPT_ID: 9.004
Field Supp. Range Unit
FloatValue This field shall be the current illumination from M Lux
the external brightness sensor.

Access Type
 Input

##### 2.7.6 Input Movement Trigger (MT)

DP Name: Movement Trigger Abbr.: MT Mandatory
FB Name: Movement Detector for Lighting Can be internal
Description
This Input shall allow for the reception of external movement signals.
It can be used as an alternative to the internal signal MSLT or be evaluated in parallel with it.
The precise point where this signal is evaluated in the FB MSLT design is not fixed: it may or may not be
subject to evaluation of IOO, brightness, timers, etc.
The functionality of the Input MT can be disabled through the Parameter Movement Trigger Evaluation
(see 2.7.10).
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Start
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.010
Field Supp. Range Unit
b 0 = Stop M {0, 1} none
This shall be interpreted as the end of the
movement detection by an external
movement sensor.
1 = Start
This shall be interpreted as the start of the
movement detection by an external
movement sensor.

Access Type

##### 2.7.7 Parameter Brightness Threshold (BT)

DP Name: Brightness Threshold Abbr.: BT Mandatory
FB Name: Movement Detector for Lighting (MDL) Can be internal
Description
This Parameter shall be the threshold value of the detected brightness above which the movement
detector will not signal detected movement, as specified in 2.2.5.
This Parameter may be implemented as well as Memory Mapped Datapoint, as Group Object or Interface
Object Property. The functionality can also be realised by a hardwired input.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Value_Lux
DPT Format: F16 DPT_ID: 9.004
Field Supp. Range Unit Default
F16 Threshold value M cs Lux none

##### 2.7.8 Parameter Output Control Time (OCT)

**FB:** MDL **Property Name (Server):** Output Control Time Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
Please refer to the functional specification.
**For the Output Timed StartStop**

The Parameter OCT shall in this case be the period of the periodic transmission of the Output TSS in
case movement is detected continuously for a longer time; see Figure 35.
**For the Output Switch OnOff**

The Parameter OCT shall in this case be the period starting with the last detection of movement and
after which the FB MDL shall switch off the light; see Figure 34.
**DPT:** **Name** DPT_TimePeriodSec **DPT_ID** 7.008 **Datatype format:** U16
**Field** **Description** **Sup.** **Range** **Unit** **Resol.:**
b Time period. M min.: 0 s s 1 s
max: none

**Communication:**

DP Address: Object Type: 414 Property ID: 110
(in the server) Start-Index: 1 N° of elements

Property access: Read only  - Read/Write
Protection Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Curr Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

##### 2.7.9 Parameter Enable Brightness Independency (EBI)

DP Name: Enable Brightness Independency Abbr.: EBI Mandatory
FB Name: Movement Detector for Lighting Can be internal
Description
This Parameter shall control (enable/disable) whether the FB MDL
 functions independent of the measured or received brightness (Input Brightness External, see 2.7.5),

and will thus switch the light actuatopr even if there is sufficient light in the room, or
 functions only if the measured or received brightness is below a given threshold.
This Parameter shall be implemented as a Group Object.
Datapoint Type
DPT_Name: DPT_Enable
DPT Format: B1 DPT_ID: 1.003
Field Supp. Range Unit
b 0 = disable (brightness is evaluated) M {0, 1} none

The FB MDL shall only evaluate and
possibly transmit detected movement if the
brightness is below the threshold.
1 = enable (brightness is not evaluated).

The FB MDL shall evaluate any detected
movement regardless of the current
brightness.

Access Type
 Input
N  this 1  this
Spontaneous Cyclically: Time-out:
Request Polling: Period:
Communication Type
 Group Object Datapoint Mandatory:
Default Group Address:
Dynamics
Power down: Save:
Power up: Value: No initialisation: Default value:
Saved value: Current value (not for input):
Transmit on bus (only for output): Read from bus (only for input):
Exception Handling
None.
Special Features
None.

##### 2.7.10 Parameter Movement Trigger Evaluation

**FB:** MDL **Property Name (Server):** Movement Trigger Evaluation Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
This Parameter shall control whether the Input Movement Trigger directly controls the Outputs SOO
and/or TSS, or is subject to one or more internal evaluation criteria, just as MSLT state, and may thus not
cause a transmission of SOO and/or TSS.
**DPT:** **Name** **DPT_ID** **Datatype format:**
**Field** **Description** **Sup.** **Range** **Unit** **Resol.:**
b 0 = disable M {0,1} none none

The Input Movement Trigger does
not directly affect the tranmission
of the Outputs SOO and/or TSS,
but is subject to one or more
internal evaluations.
1 = enable

The Input Movement Trigger shall
directly cause the transmission of
the Outputs SOO and/or TSS.

**Communication:**

DP Address: Object Type: 414 Property ID: 111
(in the server) Start-Index: 1 N° of elements

Property access: Read only  - Read/Write
Protection Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Curr Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

##### 2.7.11 Parameter Movement Sensor Pause Time

**FB:** MDL **Property Name (Server):** Movement Sensor Pause Time Mandatory
Optional
**Description:**
Please refer to the functional specification.
This Parameter shall contain the short period starting with the reception of the value On on the Input IOO,
during which the internal detection of light shall be supressed.
**DPT:** **Name** DPT_TimePeriod100Msec **DPT_ID** 7.004 **Datatype format:** U16
**Field** **Description** **Sup.** **Range** **Unit** **Resol.:**
TimePeriod This field shall contain the M min.: 0 s s 100 ms
duration of the pause time. max: none

**Communication:**

DP Address: Object Type: 414 Property ID: 112
(in the server) Start-Index: 1 N° of elements

Property access: Read only  - Read/Write
Protection Read level  - Write level  **Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Curr Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

### 3 Photometric sensors

#### 3.1 Overview photometric sensors (informative)
###### The following types of photometric sensors exist.

 1. Indoor Brightness Sensor This measures the indoor brightness.

 This is modelled by the FB Indoor Brightness Sensor (FB IBS, 409) in this paper.

 Its main Output provides the illuminance (DPT_Value_Lux, 9.004).

 2. Indoor Luminance Sensor This measures the indoor luminance.

 This is modelled by the FB Indoor Luminance Sensor (FB ILS, 410) in 3.2.

 Its main Output provides the luminance (DPT_Value_Luminance, 14.041).

 3. Daylight sensor This measures the outdoor brightness, typically in a larger range, for instance 1 000 Lux to 100 000 Lux.

 It provides the illuminance to the bus and may foresee some 1 bit Outputs for threshold functions.

 This sensor is not yet modelled as FB in KNX.

 4. Twilight sensor This measures the outdoor brightness, typically in the lower range 0 Lux to 1 000 Lux.

 It mainly provides a 1 bit Output to the bus.

 This sensor is not yet modelled as FB in KNX.

 5. Sun Intensity Sensor This sensor measures the sun intensity and provides the data to the bus with unit Wm[-2]. This information is mainly used in HVAC applications.

 This sensor is modelled in [03].


-----

#### 3.2 FB Indoor Brightness Sensor (Object Type 409)

##### 3.2.1 Aims and objectives
###### The FB Indoor Brightness Sensor (FB IBS) shall provide the illuminance measured at a certain location and provide this to the KNX system.

NOTE 5 This relates in turn to the irradiance (Wm-2) as specified in FB Sun Intensity Sensor (see [03]) weighted by the spectral
sensitivity of the human eye.

###### This shall be a physical sensor with a built-in or hard-wired brightness sensor.

##### 3.2.2 Functional specification

###### 3.2.2.1 Explanation of illuminance The illuminance is the ratio of the luminous flux indescent on a given surface and the size of that surface.

 Typical illuminance value that can be expected are listed in Table 15.

 Table 15 – Typical illuminance values

**Light conditions** **Illuminance**

Sunlight at noon in summer 100 000 Lux

Cloudy sky in summer 10 000 Lux

Rainy wheather with thunder clouds 1 000 Lux

Office lighting 500 Lux

Living room lighting 200 Lux

Staircase lighting 100 Lux

Street lighting 10 Lux

Twilight after sunset 1 Lux

Midnight at full moon 0,2 Lux

Sky with stars and no moon 0,000 5 Lux

###### 3.2.2.2 Basic functionality The FB IBS shall be able to detect the indoor brightness.

 From the measured electronic signals, the illumination shall be calculated. This calculation is not standardised. It shall lead to the value representing the illumination on a given room element. This calculated value shall be transmitted to KNX via the Output Room Illumination encoded as DPT_Value_Lux (DPT_ID: 9.004).

|Light conditions|Illuminance|
|---|---|
|Sunlight at noon in summer|100 000 Lux|
|Cloudy sky in summer|10 000 Lux|
|Rainy wheather with thunder clouds|1 000 Lux|
|Office lighting|500 Lux|
|Living room lighting|200 Lux|
|Staircase lighting|100 Lux|
|Street lighting|10 Lux|
|Twilight after sunset|1 Lux|
|Midnight at full moon|0,2 Lux|
|Sky with stars and no moon|0,000 5 Lux|


-----

###### Figure 43 – Typical room brightness measurement method

 3.2.2.3 Calibration It may be necessary that the installed device that realises the FB Brightness Sensor has to be calibrated. This may be due to:

 - the electronic measurement method, or

 - the mechanics (optics), or

 - the mounting place (e.g. in the ceiling), or

 - the reflection by objects in the room (e.g. floor, furniture, walls, etc.)

 The installer procedure for this calibration is not standardised.

##### 3.2.3 Constraints

###### 3.2.3.1 Evaluation of the calculated illuminance The FB IBS does not further evaluate the illuminance. The evaluation of threshold values or the further control of lighting is the task for different Functional Blocks.

 3.2.3.2 Luminance (cdm[-2]) This FB IBS does not feature any measurement of the luminance. The luminance shall be provided by the FB Indoor Luminance Sensor (see [03]).

 If it is wanted that both illuminance as well as luminance be provided on the bus, then both FBs Indoor Brightness Sensor and Indoor Luminance Sensor can be combined in a device.

#### 3.3 FB Indoor Luminance Sensor (Object Type 410)

##### 3.3.1 Aims and objectives
###### The FB Indoor Luminance Sensor (ILS) shall provide the luminance measured at a certain location and provides this to the KNX system.

##### 3.3.2 Functional specification

###### 3.3.2.1 Explanation of luminance Luminance is defined in [06]. It represents the luminous intensity in a certain direction.

 This quantity characterizes the impression of brightness, which an illuminated or a luminant surface effects in the human eye.

 The luminance is independent from the distance to the observer; that means, that the impression of brightness does not change when the distance between observer and observed object changes.

 Typical luminance value that can be expected are listed in Table 16.

 Table 16 – Typical luminance values

**Light source** **Luminance**

Sun at noon 1 600 000 000 cd/m²

100 W clear light bulb 10 000 000 cd/m²

Sun at sunset 5 000 000 cd/m²

100 W opal light bulb 200 000 cd/m²

Blue sky 10 000 cd/m²

Candlelight 5 000 cd/m²

Moonlight 2 500 cd/m²

sky at night 0,001 cd/m²

###### 3.3.2.2 Basic functionality The FB ILS shall be able to detect the indoor luminance.

 The luminance is typically measured by an electronic sensor.

 The measured luminance shall be provided to the KNX system through the Output Indoor Luminance (IL) encoded as DPT_Value_Luminance (14.041, F32, cdm[-2]).

##### 3.3.3 Constraints
###### None.

DP Name: Indoor Luminance Abbr.: IL Mandatory
FB Name: FB Indoor Luminance Sensor Can be internal
**Description**
This Datapoint shall represent the luminance observed by the FB ILS.
If the variation of the luminance changes more than COV then the new value shall be transmitted on the
bus. If the luminance doesn’t change more than COV, then the current value shall be transmitted
periodically.

###### 3.3.7.2 Parameter Change of Value (COV)

**FB:** ILS **Property Name (Server):** Change of Value **Mandatory**
**Optional**
**Description:**
This represents the minimal change of the measurement that send a new value on the Output IL.
**DPT:** **Name** DPT_Value_Luminance **DPT_ID** 14.041 **Datatype format:** F32
**Field** **Description** **Sup.** **Range** **Unit** **Resol.:**
F32 This field shall contain the M cs cdm[-] 1 cdm[-2]
value over which the 2
measured luminance shall
change before it is transmitted
on the bus.

**Communication:**
 Property Mandatory:
DP Address: Object Type: 410 Property ID: 110
(in the server) Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

Property access: Read only  - Read/Write
Protection Read level 3 Write level 3
**Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Curr Value Default Value

**Special Features:**
None.

###### 3.3.7.3 Parameter: Repetition Time (RT)

**FB:** ILS **Property Name (Server):** Repetition Time **Mandatory**
**Optional**
**Description:**
This represents the period of emission of the Output Indoor Luminance (IL) when no change of value is
detected.
**DPT:** **Name** DPT_TimePeriodSec **DPT_ID** 7.005 **Datatype format:** U16
**Field** **Description** **Sup.** **Range** **Unit** **Resol.:**
TimePeriod This shall specify the repetition M cs s 1 s
time of the periodic
transmission of the Output IL.

**Communication:**

DP Address: Object Type: 410 Property ID: 111
(in the server) Start-Index: 1 N° of elements 1

Property access: Read only Read/Write
Protection Read level 3 Write level 3
**Exception Handling:** Value after Power-up: Stored Value Curr Value Default Value
None.
**Special Features:**
None.

### 4 Functional Blocks for E-Mode Channels

#### 4.1 Usage requirements
###### The Functional Block specifications below only provide complementary information to the E-Mode Channel definitions. They are only provided for completeness and understanding of these E-Mode Channel definitions.

 As a consequence, no Object Types for Interface Objects are specified below. It will be a decision of KNX Association Working Group Interworking how these Functional Blocks will be continued and if any Object Type will be assigned.

 These Functional Blocks shall be used only for implementation of E-Mode devices.

 These Functional Block specifications shall not be used for any other goal; in particular, no implementation for S-Mode devices shall be based on these specifications.

 KNX Association will take care of compatibility between any currently specified E-Mode Channel definition and the final version of these Functional Blocks.

 To this, the KNX Association Application Specification Groups shall take the functionality achieved by these Functional Blocks as the minimal mandatory basis for further work.

#### 4.2 FB_Switch_Scene_Numbered

##### 4.2.1 Definition

######  Name: FB_Switch_Scene_Numbered

  Object type: See “Usage requirements” in 4.1.

##### 4.2.2 Functional specification
###### On interaction, a scene number shall be sent.

 There shall be two possible interactions.
 1. On interaction 1 the value of parameter Scene Number 1 (P1) shall be sent. 2. On interaction 2 the value of parameter Scene Number 2 (P2) shall be sent.

 It shall not be possible to learn scenes.

##### 4.2.3 Functional Block diagram

###### FB_Switch_Scene_Numbered

 Inputs Outputs (SN) Scene Number  Parameters Scene Number 1 (P1)  Scene Number 2 (P2)

#### 4.3 FB_Switch_Dimming_Value

##### 4.3.1 Definitions

######  Name: FB_Switch_Dimming_Value

  Object type: See “Usage requirements” in 4.1.

##### 4.3.2 Functional specification
###### On interactions, a dimming value shall be sent.

 There shall be two possible interactions.
 1. On interaction 1 the value parameter Dimming Value 1 (P1) shall be sent. 2. On interaction 2 the value of para meter Dimming Value 2 (P2) shall be sent.

#### 4.4 FB_PB_Dimming_Value

##### 4.4.1 Definition

######  Name: FB_PB_Dimming_Value

  Object type: See “Usage requirements” in 4.1.

##### 4.4.2 Functional specification
###### On interaction, a dimming value shal be sent.

 There shall be only one possible interaction.
 1. On interaction 1 (press on button for example) value of parameter Dimming Value (P1) shall be sent.
